findings.description: The sentence "Hooks are off for the same reason they are everywhere else in the gate (decision 28)" now describes something `runGit` does automatically. At a `runGit` call site it reads as if the hooks setting were this call's own choice. The first sentence (the timeout, held while the merge lock is taken) is a genuine WHY and should stay.

The merge target from `branch --show-current` is read from HEAD in the shared, session-writable git dir and is passed to `git rebase`/`merge-base`/`checkout` with no option terminator, so a branch name like `--exec=...` would run as a git option outside the sandbox.

gitDiffPaths trims its -z listing, which strips leading whitespace from the first changed path, so an out-of-scope path like ' src/evil.sh' reaches auditScope as 'src/evil.sh' and passes a 'src/**' scope.

`gh pr create` runs in the trusted checkout with only `scrubbedGitEnv()`. gh then runs its own git, without GIT_SAFE_CONFIG, including what I believe is an unconditional `git status --porcelain` (`UncommittedChangeCount`). A `core.fsmonitor` a session plants in the shared `$GIT_COMMON_DIR/config` would then run unsandboxed as the operator, under the merge lock. Neither `runGit` nor the source scan can see a git process that gh starts. Decision 73 keeps gh on 'the scrub without git's argv', but git also reads command-scope config from `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n` (git 2.31+), so the same disarm can reach gh through env. The same applies to the `gh pr edit` and `gh pr list` spawns in this file.
